mission: Talon identifies Korda as old GAG security system in respectable clothing. Korda’s presence implies the Foundation is operationally compromised by old GAG-linked security and records access. Talon’s humor thins out — Korda makes Talon feel contaminated by his own past, not merely suspicious. Using Iressa’s tools, Talon submits a fake manifest correction / records query that makes it look as if a missing piece of the Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest has resurfaced. The signal is boring enough to look bureaucratic, but specific enough that anyone guarding the old shipment trail will notice. This is not just hacking. Talon uses the shape of his old compromised work as bait, putting an old version of himself back on the board.
why_now: Chapter 18 occupies the attack phase and carries the next locked outline turn.
conflict: Korda should make Talon feel seen in the worst way. The bait-setting beat should feel like Talon willingly re-entering the room that ruined his life because the only way to catch the people who put him there is to look like them again. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: Plain-language consequence: if Korda responds, the Foundation is actively guarding the hidden shipment trail.
setting: Coruscant, Iressa's secondary cache (Talon submits the fake manifest correction here) and then the Foundation's external surface (where Korda responds, indirectly, through a courier dispatch). Mid-evening; the warehouse district is quiet; foot traffic is sparse.
